title: branches.py skeleton: importable CLI, JSON contract, load_format
riskReason: The new CLI runs git and reads the repo config, so a wrong contract misleads every later consumer.

seeds.title: validate_format accepts a leading dash and control or bidi characters
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts a format that starts with '-'. It also accepts control and bidi characters. No caller gives the format to git in this slice. S-002 adds git check-ref-format --branch inside validate_format, and that check rejects these values. Keep the check inside validate_format. Give every later git argument after '--' or as a full ref name.

seeds.title: GIT_MODES_PATH uses abspath, while the scripts use realpath
seeds.detail: GIT_MODES_PATH uses os.path.abspath(__file__). The three scripts use os.path.realpath for their sys.path entry. A symlinked branches.py reads the git-modes.json beside the symlink, not the real file. Use os.path.realpath here too, so one rule applies.

seeds.title: Two tests build the same skill copy
seeds.detail: The new test and 'a git-modes.json that cannot be read' in skills/sdlc/test/branches.test.mjs each copy branches.py into a scratch directory with their own code. Merge the directory and mode-000 shapes into the new shape table, or share one skillCopy helper.

seeds.title: Round-1 architecture findings still open
seeds.detail: load_git_modes has three copies (branches.py, next-action.py, state-write.py). GIT_MODES_PATH in branches.py uses abspath, but the sys.path lines use realpath. Build GIT_MODES_PATH from one realpath SKILL_DIR. The npm test glob does not reach test/testkit/*.test.mjs; widen it or import the testkit self-tests from a top-level test file.

seeds.title: No committed test pins the RecursionError catch in load_git_modes
seeds.detail: Fix round 1 added RecursionError to the except in load_git_modes (branches.py:56). The committed deep-nesting test (branches.test.mjs:257) covers config.json only. Verifier test TC-cli-21 (.sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r1/tests/cli-0/branches.verify-cli.test.mjs) covers a deeply nested git-modes.json, an empty-string mode, a null top level and a dangling symlink. The skill ships git-modes.json, so a hostile shape there is unlikely. Fix: when a later slice touches preflight, add the deep-nesting and empty-string-mode shapes to the test at branches.test.mjs:217.

seeds.title: argparse prefix abbreviation accepted
seeds.detail: allow_abbrev is on, so `parse --rep DIR` is accepted as --repo. The spec names no prefix forms of the flags.

seeds.title: Unicode digits accepted as integers
seeds.detail: type=int accepts non-ASCII digits: `--n '١'` gives n = 1. Later tails could embed a value the user did not type in ASCII.

seeds.title: Repeated flag silently takes the last value
seeds.detail: `parse --branch x --branch y` uses y and does not report bad input.

seeds.title: --help prints usage text, not JSON
seeds.detail: `branches.py parse --help` prints argparse usage text and exits 0. This breaks the one-JSON-object stdout contract for that one invocation.

seeds.title: Non-UTF-8 argv passes through as surrogate escapes
seeds.detail: `--branch $'x\xff'` is echoed as x\udcff. The later parse and name logic should decide whether this is bad input.

seeds.title: argparse accepts flag prefixes
seeds.detail: allow_abbrev is on: parse accepts --r, --re, --rep for --repo and --f to --forma for --format, exit 0 (TC-cli-7). The spec names full flags only. Set allow_abbrev=False on the parser and each subparser.

seeds.title: --n, --round and --part accept negative, huge, padded, underscore and non-ASCII digit values
seeds.detail: type=int accepts -1, 99999999999999999999, ' 3', Arabic-Indic 3, '0003', '1_000' and '+4' (TC-cli-10). Tails in spec §1 need non-negative ASCII integers. The slices that build name() should reject these.

seeds.title: A flag given twice keeps the last value silently
seeds.detail: parse --branch a --branch b exits 0 with branch b (TC-cli-6).

seeds.title: --help prints argparse usage and exits 0, not JSON
seeds.detail: --help, -h and '<command> --help' print usage text on stdout with exit 0 (TC-cli-8). A caller that parses stdout as JSON breaks on it.

seeds.title: A config.json with a UTF-8 BOM is refused
seeds.detail: load_format reads with utf-8, so a BOM gives 'Unexpected UTF-8 BOM' and exit 2 (TC-cli-19). Reading with utf-8-sig would accept it.

seeds.title: testkit: copySkill cannot turn an existing file into a directory
seeds.detail: copySkill({files: {'git-modes.json': null}}) throws EEXIST because writeFiles calls mkdirSync on the existing file. Callers must also put the path in omit.

seeds.title: branches.py --help and -h exit through SystemExit in main()
seeds.detail: main(['--help']) and main(['parse','-h']) print argparse usage text on stdout and raise SystemExit(0). An in-process caller gets an exception, not a return code, and the CLI prints usage text, not one JSON object. The spec does not define --help.

seeds.title: A UTF-8 BOM in .sdlc/config.json makes every command without --format exit 2
seeds.detail: load_format opens config.json with encoding utf-8, so a BOM gives 'Unexpected UTF-8 BOM'. Use utf-8-sig to accept it. The spec does not name this case.

seeds.title: A valid --format hides a malformed config.json
seeds.detail: With --format given, load_format is not called, so a command exits 0 while config.json is invalid JSON. Later slices that read other config keys may need to read the config anyway.

seeds.title: A decoy branches.py beside a symlink to a script shadows the real module
seeds.detail: The scripts insert os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) into sys.path. abspath does not resolve symlinks. When janitor.py runs through a symlink in a directory that also holds branches.py, that file is imported (manual probe: decoy exit 97). os.path.realpath closes this. The spec names no symlink case.

seeds.title: branches.py: a decoy branches.py beside a symlinked script wins the import
seeds.detail: The three scripts insert os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) into sys.path. abspath does not resolve symlinks. When a script runs through a symlink, a branches.py beside the symlink is imported in place of the real module (decoy exit 97 for all three scripts). os.path.realpath fixes this. The spec does not define the script directory for a symlink.

seeds.title: branches.py: main(["-h"]) raises SystemExit instead of returning
seeds.detail: main(["-h"]) and main(["parse","--help"]) print argparse usage text and raise SystemExit(0). The spec does not define -h. An importing caller gets an exception, and stdout is not a JSON object.

seeds.title: branches.py: load_format drops a non-string branchFormat, but spec section 4 uses config.get("branchFormat") or default
seeds.detail: load_format returns sdlc/{name} for a truthy non-string branchFormat such as 5. Spec section 4 describes next-action semantics as config.get("branchFormat") or "sdlc/{name}", which keeps 5. The two readings diverge when later slices thread fmt through next-action.py.

seeds.title: branches.py: validate_format accepts NUL and control characters in S-001
seeds.detail: validate_format("sdlc/{name}\x00") and validate_format("a\x01/{name}") return the input. ADR-20261009-024036 assigns git check-ref-format to S-002 (R-017). S-002 must refuse these.

seeds.title: branches.py: a valid --format succeeds although the config is malformed
seeds.detail: parse --format sdlc/{name} exits 0 when .sdlc/config.json holds truncated JSON, because the flag skips load_format. The plan asked only to record this. Preflight can report a malformed config even when the flag is given.

seeds.title: argparse accepts flag prefixes
seeds.detail: build_parser keeps allow_abbrev=True. --rep, --r, --form and --f are accepted as --repo and --format. A later flag with a shared prefix changes their meaning. Set allow_abbrev=False on the parser and the subparsers.

seeds.title: A duplicate flag keeps its last value silently
seeds.detail: --repo /nonexistent --repo R exits 0. --format bad --format sdlc/{name} also exits 0. An appended flag overrides an earlier one without notice.

seeds.title: --n, --round and --part accept unicode digits, padding, underscores and negatives
seeds.detail: type=int accepts Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits, ' 3', '1_000', '-1' and up to 4300 digits. Later slices put these values in branch names. Use a strict ^[0-9]+$ check when name lands.

seeds.title: Refusal errors echo the whole hostile value
seeds.detail: A 100000-digit --n gives a 100035-char error. A 200000-char --format gives an error of the same size. Clip the echoed value. This is for verify-limits, because the spec states no size limit.

seeds.title: -h and --help print argparse usage on stdout
seeds.detail: Help exits 0 with plain text, not one JSON object. The spec does not define help. A caller that parses stdout as JSON breaks on it.

seeds.title: load_git_modes lets OSError and RecursionError escape
seeds.detail: Make git-modes.json a directory, an unreadable file or a 200000-deep nesting. preflight then exits 1 with a traceback (IsADirectoryError, PermissionError or RecursionError). Catch OSError and RecursionError and raise Fail.

seeds.title: load_format lets RecursionError escape and blocks on a FIFO
seeds.detail: A config.json nested 200000 deep makes every command exit 1 with RecursionError. A FIFO at .sdlc/config.json blocks the command until it is killed. This is for verify-contract (VS-6) and verify-limits.

seeds.title: Invisible and confusable characters pass the format checks
seeds.detail: ZWSP, U+202E and Cyrillic letters pass validate_format. git check-ref-format also accepts them, so S-002 does not refuse them either. Such formats give branch names that read differently from their bytes. The spec does not forbid them.

seeds.title: Scripts now need branches.py beside them
seeds.detail: janitor.py, next-action.py and state-write.py import branches from their own directory. A copy of one script without branches.py fails at import. The slice updates git-modes.test.mjs for this. No other repo code copies the scripts alone.

seeds.title: branches.py resolves git-modes.json with abspath, not realpath
seeds.detail: GIT_MODES_PATH uses os.path.abspath(__file__). When branches.py runs through a symlink, preflight reads git-modes.json beside the symlink and exits 2 with 'is missing'. The three scripts now use realpath. The spec does not require a symlinked run of branches.py.

seeds.title: A --repo directory that cannot be read passes when --format is given
seeds.detail: With mode 000 on --repo, parse exits 2 without --format because the config.json read fails. It exits 0 with --format because _repo checks only os.path.isdir (TC-cli-23). Consider an os.access read check in _repo.

seeds.title: GIT_MODES_PATH still uses abspath, not realpath
seeds.detail: The fix made the three scripts resolve their directory through realpath. branches.py builds GIT_MODES_PATH from os.path.abspath(__file__). A branches.py run through a symlink in another directory reads git-modes.json beside the symlink. This seed is not tested here.

seeds.title: branches.py: load_format reports a NUL in the repo path as invalid JSON
seeds.detail: An in-process caller that passes a repo path with a NUL gets Fail with '<path> is not valid JSON: ValueError: embedded null byte'. The file is never read, so the message names the wrong cause. The CLI cannot receive a NUL in argv.

seeds.title: branches.py: a config.json with an integer over 4300 digits is refused
seeds.detail: Valid JSON with a 5000-digit integer in any key makes load_format raise Fail because of the Python int digits limit, although branchFormat is valid. This is an unlikely config.

seeds.title: An in-process caller with a cached branches module binds it, not the skill's module
seeds.detail: When a process already holds sys.modules['branches'], a script loaded through importlib binds that cached module and ignores the sys.path line (A-31). A test harness that imports another branches.py and then loads next-action.py in the same process tests the wrong module. Repo callers load each script in a new process today, so nothing breaks. Keep that rule for later probes.

seeds.title: branches.py resolves git-modes.json through abspath, not realpath
seeds.detail: GIT_MODES_PATH uses os.path.abspath(__file__). When branches.py runs through a symlink, preflight reads git-modes.json beside the symlink and exits 2 with 'is missing'. The three scripts use realpath. The spec does not require a symlinked run of branches.py.

title: validate_format, split and name
riskReason: validate_format calls git check-ref-format; a wrong pass admits formats whose names the forge rejects.

seeds.title: Branch formats with shell characters pass validation
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts 'sdlc/{name}$(id)' and 'sdlc/{name};rm' because git allows these characters. I ran both. The spec delegates validity to git and the forge, so this is not a defect in S-002. Later slices that put a branch name into a shell string must quote it, or use an argument list.

seeds.title: name() does not check the tail
seeds.detail: An id such as '../x' gives 'sdlc/../x'. Today only validate_format and the tests call name, with a fixed id. Slices that feed ledger ids or CLI input into name (S-004 and later) must check the result before git or a path uses it.

seeds.title: Invisible characters pass validation
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts U+200B because git allows it. I ran 'sdlc/​{name}' and it passed. Such a format gives names that look the same as other names. The spec gives this job to git and the forge rules, so this note is for information only.

seeds.title: KINDS and TAILS list the branch kinds twice
seeds.detail: KINDS and TAILS both list the branch kinds. _kind accepts a kind that tail refuses until S-004 to S-006 add all rows. Fix: when the table is complete, derive KINDS from TAILS, or assert in a test that the two sets are equal.

seeds.title: TAILS constant sits between functions
seeds.detail: TAILS sits between validate_format and tail. The module keeps its other constants at the top. Fix: move TAILS next to KINDS and PLACEHOLDERS.

seeds.title: T-012 name promises a whitespace case it does not test
seeds.detail: The case sdlc/{ name } holds no placeholder, so it fails at the placeholder count, not at the whitespace check. T-018 now pins the whitespace check, so only the name is wrong. Fix: replace the case with 'sdlc/ {name}', or rename the test to say it covers a malformed placeholder.

seeds.title: T-018 tab case does not match the test name
seeds.detail: Git refuses 'sdlc/\tS-001' (exit 128), but the test name says 'Unicode whitespace that git accepts'. Git accepts U+00A0, U+3000 and U+2028. Fix: drop the tab case, or rename the test to 'rejects Unicode and control whitespace'.

seeds.title: Whitespace branch of validate_format has no direct Python test
seeds.detail: sdlc/{ name } fails at the placeholder count, not at the whitespace check. The whitespace branch is reached only by the S-001 CLI case 'sdlc/ {name}'. Add a direct Python case such as 'sdlc /{name}' to pin it.

seeds.title: tail accepts extra parts silently
seeds.detail: tail('slice', id='S-1', extra=1) returns 'S-1' and does not raise Fail. The spec does not say whether extra parts are an error.

seeds.title: A git binary on PATH decides the format verdict
seeds.detail: validate_format runs the first git on PATH. A fake git that exits 0 admits sdlc/{name}.. (TC-cli-11). The spec does not pin the git binary.

seeds.title: Zero-width characters pass validate_format
seeds.detail: U+200B, U+200D and U+FEFF do not match Python \s, and git accepts them, so a​b/{name} is valid (TC-cli-5). The branch names then look the same as names without these characters.

seeds.title: Control characters U+001C to U+001F are reported as whitespace
seeds.detail: Python \s matches U+001C to U+001F, so a\x1f/{name} fails with 'holds whitespace', not with the git reason. The verdict is correct, but the message names the wrong cause.

seeds.title: testkit: cli-runner has no per-run absolute python option
seeds.detail: A test that isolates PATH must build a second runner with cliRunner({ python: <abs path> }), because python3 is found through the child PATH.

seeds.title: Zero-width and BOM characters pass validate_format
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts formats with U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF and U+180E. These characters are not Unicode whitespace, and git accepts them, so a branch name can hold an invisible character. The spec forbids only whitespace. Consider refusing Unicode format characters (category Cf).

seeds.title: The first git on PATH decides the validate_format verdict
seeds.detail: A fake git on PATH that exits 0 makes validate_format accept sdlc/{name}... The spec does not define which git runs. Consider naming the git binary in the pre-flight output.

seeds.title: Control characters U+001C to U+001F fail as whitespace
seeds.detail: Python re \s matches U+001C to U+001F. validate_format therefore refuses a\x1f/{name} with the message 'holds whitespace', not with the git control-character reason. The verdict is correct. Only the message text is misleading.

seeds.title: name accepts a non-string id and stringifies it
seeds.detail: name("sdlc/{name}", "slice", id=False) gives sdlc/False, id=[] gives sdlc/[] and id={} gives sdlc/{}. tail checks only None and the empty string. A Fail for an id that is not a str keeps such names out of git.

seeds.title: name does not check the id text against git
seeds.detail: name gives sdlc/.., 'sdlc/ ' and sdlc/S-001.lock without Fail. validate_format checks only the sample id S-001. A caller that passes an operator id gets a name that git check-ref-format refuses later.

seeds.title: an unhashable kind raises TypeError, not Fail
seeds.detail: tail uses TAILS.get(kind), so a list or a dict kind raises TypeError. Every other unknown kind raises Fail. An isinstance check on kind makes the Fail contract total.

seeds.title: testkit: pycall cannot pass keyword arguments
seeds.detail: callPython calls fn(*args) only. name and tail take **parts, so the verifier wrote a shim module with name_kw(fmt, kind, parts). A kwargs field in the pycall request removes the shim.

seeds.title: Invisible and terminal-control characters pass the format check
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF, U+2060, U+180E and C1 U+009B (CSI) in the literal part, because git accepts them. A branch name can then look the same as another name or carry a terminal escape. The spec delegates this check to git, so it is not a defect.

seeds.title: Formats that start with refs/heads/, HEAD or @ pass
seeds.detail: refs/heads/{name}, refs/{name}, HEAD{name} and @{name} pass git check-ref-format --branch. refs/heads/{name} gives the branch refs/heads/refs/heads/S-001, which is ambiguous with refs.

seeds.title: A lone surrogate in a Python-side format passes
seeds.detail: validate_format('a\udc80/{name}') returns the format. Python passes byte 0x80 to git, and git accepts it. The format is not valid Unicode, so later JSON or forge calls can treat it differently.

seeds.title: S-001 TC-* evidence tests are missing
seeds.detail: The evidence.tests of R-014, R-016 and R-098 list TC-* tests under .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r1/tests/. Those files exist in neither the branch nor the main tree, so no lens can run them again.

seeds.title: T-012 whitespace case reaches the placeholder check, not the whitespace check
seeds.detail: The T-012 case sdlc/{ name } raises Fail at the placeholder count (found 0). T-018 now covers the whitespace branch, so only the T-012 case name is misleading.

seeds.title: tail accepts extra parts
seeds.detail: tail('slice', id='S-1', extra=1) returns S-1 and raises no Fail. The spec does not say whether extra parts are an error.

title: tail contract and format resolution order
riskReason: The resolution order decides which format every branch gets; a wrong order silently renames future branches.

seeds.title: name does not check the parts it puts in the branch name
seeds.detail: Carried from round 0. `name --kind slice --id=-c --format '{name}'` prints the branch `-c` with exit 0, and git can read it as an option. `name --kind e2e-area --id M-1 --area '../x y'` prints `sdlc/M-1-e2e-../x y` with exit 0. validate_format checks only the S-001 sample. The spec does not ask for a part check, and the parts come from ledger ids, so this is hardening. Fix: in cmd_name, run the built branch through `git check-ref-format --branch`. Consumers must put `--` before a branch name in git commands.

seeds.title: cmd_preflight reads config twice; given depends on operand order
seeds.detail: _format reads config.json through load_format, and given reads it again through _config_format. Swapping the operands of the given expression makes preflight with --format fail on a broken config. T-024 now guards this. Fix: read _config_format(repo) one time only when --format is absent, and derive fmt and given from that one value.

seeds.title: NAME_PARTS repeats the name sub-parser part flags
seeds.detail: A new part flag must change two places. Fix: build the name sub-parser part flags from NAME_PARTS, or keep the two side by side.

seeds.title: brokenConfigRepos overlaps existing broken-config fixtures
seeds.detail: The new fixture builds invalid JSON and deep-nesting configs that the deep-nesting test and withConfig also build. Fix: when a later slice needs broken configs, reuse brokenConfigRepos instead of a new fixture.

seeds.title: T-024 does not restore the mode of the unreadable config
seeds.detail: The git-modes test restores the file mode to 0o644 in a finally block. T-024 leaves config.json at mode 000. Scratch cleanup still removes it, so nothing fails now, but the two tests are not consistent. Restore the mode in a finally block.

seeds.title: T-019 still has no case for an empty ts
seeds.detail: Round 0 reported this gap. The plan says the state tail treats an empty ts as absent. Add tail("state", ts="") to T-019 and assert ^state-\d{14}$.

seeds.title: Fail message article
seeds.detail: tail's Fail message reads 'a e2e-area branch name needs a non-empty ...'. The article before a vowel is wrong. The spec does not define this text.

seeds.title: branches.py --help prints argparse text, not JSON
seeds.detail: branches.py name --help prints the argparse usage text and exits 0. The spec does not define --help, so this is not a defect. A caller that parses stdout as JSON gets text here.

seeds.title: preflight output still echoes an interim args object
seeds.detail: preflight prints {ok, command, format, args, given}. The args echo holds the absolute repo path. A later slice that defines the preflight output must decide whether args stays.

seeds.title: The missing-part error says 'a e2e-area branch name'
seeds.detail: The message puts the article 'a' before every kind. The meaning is correct, but the text reads badly for e2e-area.

seeds.title: name gives a branch that git refuses for a part with git-unsafe characters
seeds.detail: validate_format checks only the format, with the sample id S-001. name does not run git check-ref-format on the full name. The ids ../x, 'a b', x..y, x~1, a:b, x.lock, * and @{1} give branches that git refuses, and name still exits 0. The spec validates only the format. A later slice that creates branches from these names must check them. Transcripts: .sdlc/slices/S-003/verification/r0/logs/cli-1-seeds.txt.

seeds.title: the integer flags take unicode digits, padded values and underscores
seeds.detail: argparse type=int uses Python int(). So --n=٣, --n=１２, --n=' 3 ', --n=1_000, --n=+1 and --n=9223372036854775808 all exit 0. No S-003 row consumes these parts. When the verify and attempt rows land in S-004 to S-006, --n=٣ and --n=3 will give the same branch. Decide whether that is the intended result. List: .sdlc/slices/S-003/verification/r0/logs/cli-1-TC-cli-105-accepted.txt.

seeds.title: name --help prints plain help text and exits 0, not one JSON object
seeds.detail: branches.py name --help prints the argparse usage text and exits 0. Every other path prints one JSON object. The spec does not define --help. A caller that parses stdout as JSON fails on this output. A flag-like part value never reaches this path (TC-cli-104).

seeds.title: branches.py exposes helpers the spec does not name
seeds.detail: cmd_name, cmd_parse, cmd_list, cmd_preflight, build_parser, JsonArgumentParser, NAME_PARTS, TAILS and the imported datetime and timezone are public names. The spec API names only load_format, validate_format, tail, name, split, parse, list_kind, read_rules, evaluate and derive. Prefix the helpers with an underscore, or declare __all__.

seeds.title: load_format accepts the non-standard JSON values NaN and Infinity
seeds.detail: A config.json whose text is NaN or Infinity, or {"branchFormat": NaN}, gives the default and not a Fail. A config file with a UTF-8 BOM gives a Fail. No requirement covers these shapes.

seeds.title: testkit: callPython has no keyword arguments and no TZ control
seeds.detail: callPython passes positional arguments only and fixes the environment. tail and name take keyword parts, and the state check needs TZ. The contract tests use a small local consumer helper. Add kwargs and env options to callPython.

seeds.title: tail accepts a non-string part and a non-digit ts
seeds.detail: tail('slice', id=0) returns '0', and tail('state', ts='abc') returns 'state-abc'. The later parse() reads state tails with ^state-(\d{14})$, so it does not classify a branch made from a non-digit ts.

seeds.title: name gives git-invalid branch names for hostile parts
seeds.detail: name does not run git check-ref-format on the full name. --id '../..', 'a b', 'HEAD@{1}', '*' or a tab give exit 0 with branches that git check-ref-format --branch refuses. The spec validates only the format.

seeds.title: integer flags accept unicode digits, padding and underscores
seeds.detail: argparse type=int uses Python int(), so '٣', '１２', ' 3 ', NBSP-padded 3 and '1_000' are accepted. When n, round or part reach a branch name in S-004 to S-006, the name can differ from the operator's text.

seeds.title: invalid UTF-8 in a part gives lone surrogate escapes in the JSON output
seeds.detail: Raw bytes \xff\xfe in --id give branch 'sdlc/\udcff\udcfe' with exit 0. Strict JSON readers can refuse or replace lone surrogates.

seeds.title: argparse error echoes an oversized value in full
seeds.detail: --round with 100000 digits gives one JSON error that holds all the digits. The spec states no limit, so this seed goes to verify-limits.

seeds.title: testkit: cli-runner cannot pass raw bytes in argv
seeds.detail: Node spawn takes only strings, so a test with invalid UTF-8 argv needs a Python relay. A run option for byte arguments would remove that relay.

seeds.title: Done-requirement evidence points at pruned verification tests
seeds.detail: requirements.json evidence.tests for R-001, R-014, R-016, R-017, R-019, R-020, R-071 and R-098 cite TC-* files under .sdlc/slices/S-00x/verification/. The retention prune deleted those files, so later regression runs cannot re-run that evidence.

seeds.title: Wrong article in the missing-part Fail message
seeds.detail: The message reads 'a e2e-area branch name needs ...'. The spec does not define the message text.

title: tails: run, slice, milestone, e2e, e2e-area
riskReason: Wrong tails produce wrong names for the pushed run, slice, milestone and e2e families.

seeds.title: name output is not checked as a valid ref or a non-flag
seeds.detail: The new run, milestone and e2e rows build the tail from the given part with no shape check (ADR-20261009-045048 accepts this). A --id that holds '..', '~', ':', a space or a leading '-' gives a name that is not a valid ref. Under a plain '{name}' format, that name can also read as a git flag. No consumer calls name before S-008, and the loop passes only ledger ids, so the risk is low now. Fix: when consumers are wired, pass branch names to git after '--', or check the output of name with 'git check-ref-format --branch'.

seeds.title: The run_lower case in T-027 does not prove lowercasing
seeds.detail: The tail run-1 is already lowercase, so the case passes with or without {name:lower} support. Only e2e_lower proves it. Fix: remove run_lower, or do not count it as a lowercase check.

seeds.title: The empty-part cases are not the same for each new row
seeds.detail: T-026 checks an empty id only for milestone. It does not check tail('e2e', id='') or tail('run', n=''). The shared loop in tail covers them now, but a per-row builder would not. Fix: add e2e_empty_id and run_empty_n to the T-026 table.

seeds.title: T-027 makes a second copy of the CLI missing-part loop
seeds.detail: The test 'name without a required part exits 2 with one JSON error and no traceback' (line 474) has the same loop for slice and e2e-area. Fix: add the run, milestone and e2e rows to that table. Keep only the API format cases in T-027.

seeds.title: Accepted milestone ids and e2e areas give branches git check-ref-format refuses
seeds.detail: 109 of 270 accepted hostile values give a branch that git refuses, for example sdlc/../.., an id with a space, or an area with a newline. The format check probes only S-001. ADR-20261009-045048 accepts this gap. A consumer that pushes such a name fails late, at git. The list is in .sdlc/slices/S-004/verification/r0/logs/cli-0-TC-cli-9-git-refused.txt.

seeds.title: Run counter accepts unicode digits, padding and a negative sign
seeds.detail: argparse int accepts ' 3', '+1', '1_000', Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits, and -1. The value -1 gives sdlc/run--1 (ADR-20261009-045048). A counter of 4301 digits exits 2 only because of the Python int string limit, and the error echoes the full value.

seeds.title: Error text uses 'a e2e' and 'a e2e-area'
seeds.detail: The missing-part error reads 'a e2e branch name needs a non-empty id'. The article is wrong before a vowel sound. The defect is cosmetic.

seeds.title: tail('run', n=10**5000) raises ValueError, not Fail
seeds.detail: Python limits int-to-str conversion to 4300 digits. The f-string in the run builder raises ValueError for a larger int. The CLI cannot reach it, because argparse refuses the same value. An API caller gets an exception outside the Fail contract.

seeds.title: The CLI accepts a 4300-digit --n and prints a 4309-character branch
seeds.detail: git check-ref-format accepts the name. A loose ref file name over 255 bytes cannot exist on common file systems. The loop passes counters from 1, so this is a robustness gap only.

seeds.title: tail('run', n=...) accepts any type
seeds.detail: n=True gives run-True, n=1.5 gives run-1.5, n=[] gives run-[]. ADR-20261009-045048 accepts no shape check. The parse row ^run-(\d+)$ cannot read these names back. S-007 owns the round trip.

seeds.title: branches.py name prints branch names that git refuses for a hostile milestone id or e2e area
seeds.detail: name --kind milestone, e2e and e2e-area accept an id or area with '..', a space, a control character, braces or a leading slash. In 144 of 380 combinations, the printed branch fails git check-ref-format --branch, for example sdlc/../.. and sdlc/$(touch pwned). ADR-20261009-045048 accepts this gap. A git check-ref-format check of the final branch, or an id shape check, closes it. List: .sdlc/slices/S-004/verification/r0/logs/security-0-vs5-git-refused.txt.

seeds.title: tail('run', n=<int over 4300 digits>) raises ValueError, not Fail
seeds.detail: tail builds f'run-{n}', and Python refuses to print an int over 4300 digits, so tail raises ValueError. The CLI cannot reach this, because argparse int refuses the same digit count. Probe: .sdlc/slices/S-004/verification/r0/logs/security-0-seed-huge-n-api.txt.

seeds.title: --n accepts padded, signed, underscored and non-ASCII digit forms
seeds.detail: argparse int accepts ' 3 ', '+1', '-0', '1_000', '010' and Arabic-Indic or fullwidth digits, and name prints the normalized ASCII number. The branch is valid, but the CLI does not report a typo.

seeds.title: The tail error text says 'a e2e branch name'
seeds.detail: The Fail message puts the article 'a' before e2e and e2e-area. The message is clear but not grammatical.

seeds.title: Branch names are not checked as valid refs
seeds.detail: name() does not run git check-ref-format on its output. tail() checks only for a missing or empty part. A --profile or --id with '..', '~', ':', a space or a leading '-' gives a name that is not a valid ref, or that reads as a flag under a plain {name} format. The loop passes only ledger ids and planner profile names, so the risk is low now. The S-004 review has the same open point. Fix: when S-008 wires consumers, pass names to git after '--', or check the output of name with 'git check-ref-format --branch'.

seeds.title: The utc helper occurs twice in branches.test.mjs
seeds.detail: The new test 'name --kind state prints sdlc/state- and the current UTC time' defines the same utc arrow function as 'the state tail is the current UTC time'. Move it to one helper at file scope and use it in both tests.

seeds.title: New CLI state test overlaps existing state tests
seeds.detail: The test 'name --kind state prints sdlc/state- and the current UTC time' overlaps two tests. 'the state tail is the current UTC time' pins the UTC window under TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati. The name output test pins the CLI shape sdlc/state-<14 digits>. The new test adds only the UTC window through the CLI. Fold the range check into the existing CLI state assertion in a later change.

seeds.detail: Only the Python API pins a missing verify --id, --round or --part. The CLI test has one verify row, for --profile. Add CLI rows for the other three parts when a later slice touches this test.

seeds.title: verify profile accepted by name but not by the spec parse regex
seeds.detail: name accepts a profile such as Http_API and gives sdlc/S-001-v0-Http_API-0. The spec section 2 parse row for verify matches only [a-z0-9-]+? as the profile, so this name does not parse back to verify. The parse and round-trip slice owns this.

seeds.title: Grammar in the attempt missing-part error
seeds.detail: The error reads 'a attempt branch name needs a non-empty n'. It still names the part, so no requirement breaks.

seeds.title: name returns ref-unsafe verify and attempt names for hostile --profile and --id
seeds.detail: --profile ../x gives sdlc/S-001-v0-../x-0 with exit 0, and git check-ref-format refuses it. Spaces, ~, @{, : and .lock in an id do the same. No requirement bounds the parts.

seeds.title: Integer parts accept unicode digits, whitespace and huge values
seeds.detail: --part ٣, --n １２, --round ' 3' and 9999... are accepted and changed to ASCII, so two inputs give one branch name. Negative values give names such as sdlc/S-001-attempt--1.

seeds.title: Error text says 'a attempt branch name'
seeds.detail: The missing-part error for the attempt kind reads 'a attempt branch name needs a non-empty n'. The article before a vowel is wrong.

seeds.title: tail and name return ref names git refuses for hostile verify profiles and attempt ids
seeds.detail: Through the Python API, profile or id values such as '../x', 'a b', 'a~1', 'a:b', 'a@{1}', ESC and TAB give names that git check-ref-format refuses (26 of 34 calls). No S-005a requirement covers this.

seeds.title: verify and attempt parts accept non-integer and negative values through the API
seeds.detail: round=-1 gives S-001-v-1-..., round=False gives vFalse, round=1.5 gives v1.5, n=-1 gives attempt--1. A later parse slice (R-068) cannot reverse these forms.

seeds.title: an explicit state ts is not checked for 14 digits
seeds.detail: The API uses ts values such as '../../x', 'a/b', '2026\n', True and lists as given. The spec says only that the value is used as given.

seeds.detail: The evidence.tests for R-001 and other branches.py requirements cite .sdlc/slices/S-001..S-004/verification/*/tests/*.mjs. These files are in neither the branch nor the main tree, so no one can re-run them. Also, the T-025, T-026 and T-027 evidence names still use the old test titles, and S-005a renamed those tests.

seeds.detail: T-R-120a looks at a 4-line window around a push line and matches by kind name. The plan records this limit, and T-R-120b proves the scan can fail. S-009 and S-021 to S-024 must tighten it to the parsed kind. Non-blocking.

seeds.title: R-120 scan names the kind, not the parsed kind
seeds.detail: A push that builds an e2e-area branch through a variable, or a statement longer than 4 lines, passes the scan. Tighten it once parse exists (S-009, S-021 to S-024).

seeds.title: R-120 scan misses list-form gh pr create
seeds.detail: PUSH_SITE matches the text 'pr create'. A call written as run(repo, 'gh', 'pr', 'create', '--head', x) has no such text, so it is not a site.

seeds.detail: A variable-built branch, an e2e-area name more than 3 lines after the push line, and the prompts are not scanned. S-009 and S-021 to S-024 must tighten the scan to the parsed kind.

title: parse classifies a branch tail
riskReason: parse decides what counts as a loop branch; a wrong null hides an active slice from the loop.

seeds.title: Huge digit run crashes parse CLI
seeds.detail: int() on a digit run over 4300 digits raises ValueError, and the parse command prints a traceback, not JSON. Catch ValueError in parse and return None, or cap the digit count. Real git refs rarely reach this length.

seeds.title: Trailing newline matches row regexes
seeds.detail: The row regexes end in $, which matches before a trailing newline. The spec gives the same text. Callers must not pass names with a newline.

seeds.title: Case-fold logic is spelled twice in parse
seeds.detail: parse lowercases head, foot, prefix and suffix by hand, and lowercases again in the ids lookup. A small helper such as fold(text, lower) would remove the repeats. This is a style point only. Behavior matches spec section 2.

seeds.title: T-R-069a overlaps T-R-021a and T-R-024a
seeds.detail: T-R-069a repeats the three null cases of T-R-021a and the ids case of T-R-024a. R-069 requires a named test, so keep it. Optionally link the cases to cut the overlap.

seeds.title: Non-ASCII digits not pinned
seeds.detail: No test pins behavior for non-ASCII digits in run, state and verify tails. The plan records this risk and accepts it.

seeds.title: Lowercase length change in prefix gives wrong null
seeds.detail: Under {name:lower}, parse reassigns prefix to prefix.lower() before it slices the tail. A prefix with a character whose lowercase form is longer (for example İ) shifts the slice, and parse('İ/{name:lower}', 'İ/s-001') gives None. validate_format accepts that format. The spec does not cover this case.

seeds.title: Trailing newline accepted in a tail
seeds.detail: parse('sdlc/{name}', 'sdlc/S-001\n') returns a slice with tail 'S-001\n', because $ matches before a final newline. This follows the spec regex with re.search; a stricter match is a hardening choice.

seeds.title: plan note for VS-4 is wrong about run-2
seeds.detail: Row 1 is the lowercase literal run-, so run-2 classifies under the plain format too. No product defect.

seeds.title: a branch starting with a dash cannot pass as '--branch -x'
seeds.detail: argparse reads it as a flag and exits 2 with ok:false. '--branch=-x' works. Git refuses such branch names, so this is cosmetic.

seeds.title: slice row accepts any S- tail
seeds.detail: Row 8 is ^(S-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)$ as in the spec. Tails such as S-001-v-x-0 or S-001-attempt- classify as a slice with the whole tail as id.

seeds.title: spec text silent on case of prefix and suffix under lower
seeds.detail: Code compares prefix and suffix without case under {name:lower}; spec only says the row regexes get re.IGNORECASE. Plan notes say this is intended. Tests TC-contract-6 and 7 pin it.

seeds.title: row 6 takes attempt-like tails as verify
seeds.detail: S-001-v0-x-0-attempt-4 parses as verify (profile x-0-attempt, part 4) because row 6 precedes row 7. This follows the table order; no live branch name is affected.

seeds.title: parse raises ValueError for a run number of more than 4300 digits
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-<5000 digits> matches row 1. int() then raises ValueError (Python digit limit). The parse command would end with a traceback. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: parse raises AttributeError for non-string ledger ids under {name:lower}
seeds.detail: ids=[5,'S-001'] or [None] under a lower format raises AttributeError. Under a plain format it does not raise. ids=5 raises TypeError. A bare string iterates characters. These inputs are out of contract.

seeds.title: row 6 regex backtracks quadratically on long tails
seeds.detail: A tail a-v1-a-v1-... followed by '!' costs about 45 ms at 8000 characters and about 1.1 s at 40000 (1.98 s under lower). A real git branch name is far shorter. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: non-ASCII digits and a trailing newline classify
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-<ARABIC-INDIC 3> gives run n=3. sdlc/run-2<LF> gives run n=2 with the newline in tail. Both follow the spec regex text. A stricter reader may want them rejected.

seeds.title: U+017F folds to s under re.IGNORECASE
seeds.detail: Under {name:lower}, sdlc/<U+017F>-001 classifies as a slice with that id. The prefix and suffix compare uses str.lower(), which folds differently from the regex. This follows the spec text.

seeds.title: parse accepts a branch with a final newline
seeds.detail: Row regexes end in $ and use re.search, so run-2 plus a newline classifies as run. Git refs cannot hold a newline.

seeds.title: parse accepts non-ASCII digits
seeds.detail: \d matches Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits and int() converts them: run-٣ gives n 3.

seeds.title: parse raises ValueError on digit runs over 4300 characters
seeds.detail: int() hits the Python limit for run n, verify round and part, and attempt n. Low risk: a git ref cannot hold such a branch.

seeds.title: verify row backtracks quadratically on long tails
seeds.detail: 100000 characters of v0-a- repeated took 7.6 s; 200000 took 30 s. Send to verify-limits. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: parse raises on non-string items in ids
seeds.detail: None or a list as an ids item raises AttributeError from .lower(). A bare string as ids iterates by character.

seeds.title: verify id accepts NUL and any character
seeds.detail: Table row 6 uses (.+) for the id, so a NUL in the tail goes into the id.

title: parse precedence: run, milestone, e2e, e2e-area rows
riskReason: Precedence mistakes misclassify milestone and e2e branches and corrupt the loop's decisions.

seeds.title: Int digit limit removed
seeds.detail: set_int_max_str_digits(0) removes the Python int limit, so a very long digit tail in run-N costs more time to convert. Git ref length limits the risk. Optionally cap the digit count in the run and attempt rows.

seeds.title: Loose anchors and Unicode digits
seeds.detail: The $ anchor accepts a trailing newline and \d accepts Unicode digits. The spec gives these regexes and git refuses newlines in ref names. Use \Z and [0-9] if the spec changes.

seeds.title: Process-wide sys.set_int_max_str_digits(0) removes a safety limit
seeds.detail: branches.py disables the interpreter's int-string limit for the whole process so that `run-<5000 digits>` parses to a huge int. A hostile branch name with a very long digit string then costs quadratic CPU, and the parsed `n` is meaningless. Prefer keeping `n` bounded: add `\d{1,9}` to the run, attempt and verify rows, or keep the digits as a string past a limit. Then the global call goes away. Not blocking because branch names are short in practice.

seeds.title: T-R-120a/b source-scan tests are outside the slice plan and are brittle
seeds.detail: The tests scan source text for push-site lines with a regex and for the substring `-e2e-`. They are not in plan.md or tests.md for S-008 and they test text rather than behavior. They can fail on harmless edits to loop sources. Move them to the slice that owns R-120, or record them in tests.md.

seeds.title: T-R-102a to T-R-105a are a good fit with the spec
seeds.detail: The row order, anchors and boundary cases match the spec's parse table. Product code in branches.py matches the PARSE_ROWS order. No change needed.

seeds.title: tests.md lists only 8 of the added tests

seeds.title: Huge-digit test covers run row only

seeds.title: Trailing newline accepted by parse
seeds.detail: Python $ matches before a trailing newline, so sdlc/run-3\n parses as run and sdlc/M-2-e2e\n as e2e. The spec regexes use $, so this follows the spec. Consider \Z or fullmatch as hardening.

seeds.title: Unicode digits and slash in area accepted
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-٣ gives n 3. sdlc/M-2-e2e-a/b gives area a/b. The slash case follows ADR-20261009-173303-decision-judge-S-008-a88a. The spec says areas never contain slash but gives no check.

seeds.title: parse accepts a trailing newline

Python $ matches before a final newline: sdlc/M-2

seeds.title: parse treats unicode digits as digits
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-٣ gives n 3 and sdlc/M-٢ gives milestone, because \d matches non-ASCII digits. The plan keeps this behavior.

seeds.title: slash in an area is accepted (note only)
seeds.detail: sdlc/M-2-e2e-a/b gives e2e-area with area a/b. ADR-20261009-173303-decision-judge-S-008-a88a keeps this.

seeds.title: surface: list_kind, read_rules, evaluate, derive absent
seeds.detail: The spec section 2 lists these in the module API. This slice does not own them.

seeds.title: parse accepts a trailing newline on every row
seeds.detail: Python $ matches before a final newline, so M-2 followed by a newline parses as milestone. This follows the spec regexes. The security profile covers it in VS-7.

seeds.title: parse raises ValueError for run-N or attempt-N with more than 4300 digits
seeds.detail: int(value) hits Python's int string limit. The CLI prints a traceback and no JSON, against spec section 2 'every command prints one JSON object'. Guard the conversion or cap the digits. No R-102 to R-105 text covers it.

seeds.title: Trailing newline accepted by $ in rows 1 to 4
seeds.detail: parse('sdlc/{name}','sdlc/run-3\n') gives kind run. Use re.fullmatch or \Z. Real branches cannot hold a newline, so impact is low.

seeds.title: Unicode digits accepted in run-N and M-N
seeds.detail: Python \d matches non-ASCII digits, so run-٣ is n 3 and M-２ is a milestone with a non-ASCII id. Use [0-9] or re.ASCII.

seeds.title: Slash in an e2e-area tail is classified as e2e-area
seeds.detail: M-2-e2e-a/b gives area a/b. ADR-20261009-173303-decision-judge-S-008-a88a keeps this S-007 behavior.

seeds.title: parse accepts a trailing newline
seeds.detail: Python $ matches before a final newline, so M-2 followed by a newline gives milestone. Git refuses such names. Unchanged from round 0.

seeds.title: parse treats unicode digits as digits
seeds.detail: run-٣ gives n 3 and M-٢ gives a milestone. The plan keeps this.

seeds.title: slash in an area is accepted (note only)
seeds.detail: M-2-e2e-a/b gives e2e-area with area a/b, per ADR-20261009-173303-decision-judge-S-008-a88a.

seeds.title: the fix lifts the int string limit for the whole process
seeds.detail: branches.py calls sys.set_int_max_str_digits(0) at import, so any importer loses the limit. No slowdown shows at 100000 digits (137 ms). A cap on digit count would keep the limit.

seeds.title: state row accepts a trailing newline and non-ASCII digits

seeds.title: Trailing newline accepted by rows 5 to 8

seeds.title: Non-ASCII digits accepted by \d

seeds.title: Attempt and verify rows accept any id text
seeds.detail: sdlc/--flag-attempt-1 and ids with NUL or lone surrogate parse as attempt. Callers must treat id as untrusted.

seeds.title: verify row accepts a trailing newline
seeds.detail: parse of sdlc/S-001-v0-cli-0 followed by a newline gives kind verify, because $ matches before a final newline. The newline stays in tail. Same open item as S-007.

seeds.title: Verify id is not checked against the slice id shape
seeds.detail: --force-v0-cli-0 and s-001-v0-cli-0 parse as verify with a flag-like or lower-case id, as the (.+) regex allows. Callers must use the known flag.

seeds.title: testkit: callPython hangs intermittently on a 200 kB input
seeds.detail: One run in about six of the same call timed out under node spawnSync. The same call never timed out from Python in 60 runs. Parse took 3 ms.

title: list enumerates local branches of one kind
riskReason: list feeds run-branch numbering; a wrong list reuses or skips run numbers across launches.

seeds.title: Subprocess pattern duplicated
seeds.detail: _git repeats the run-and-catch pattern of validate_format. A shared helper would remove the copy. Not needed now.

seeds.title: Constant placement
seeds.detail: NUMERIC_SORT_KINDS sits mid-file, away from PARSE_ROWS and the other module constants. Move it up for consistency.

seeds.title: T-R-094b repeats T-R-094a
seeds.detail: T-R-094b asserts the same 2-before-10 order that T-R-094a already pins. The plan requires both tests. Merge them in a later slice.

seeds.title: list ignores a checked-out unborn branch
seeds.detail: In a repo with no commit where HEAD points at sdlc/S-001, list --kind slice returns []. This follows from for-each-ref and from the plan, which says an empty repo gives []. No action is needed unless a caller expects the unborn branch.

seeds.title: testkit: fixtures with case-only branch names fail on case-insensitive file systems
seeds.detail: On macOS, git refuses two branches that differ only by case, such as feature/PROJ-1-S-001 and feature/proj-1-s-001. A {name:lower} fixture needs a distinct name. This is not a product defect.

seeds.title: Non-ASCII Unicode digits count as digits in loop branch names
seeds.detail: The parse regexes use \d without re.ASCII, so sdlc/run-١ and sdlc/run-１０ list as run with n 1 and 10. 46 such names were classified across run, attempt, state, verify and milestone. Later run numbering reads this list.

seeds.title: run and state entries have no id key
seeds.detail: parse gives no id for run and state, so branches[].id is absent for those kinds. This matches ADR bd10. A caller that reads id must skip them.

seeds.title: Malformed attempt names list as slice
seeds.detail: sdlc/S-001-attempt-x and sdlc/S-001-attempt- match the slice row of the table, so list --kind slice returns them with an odd id. This follows the table.

seeds.title: list_kind returns [] for an unknown kind through the API
seeds.detail: The CLI rejects an unknown kind with exit 2. The API returns an empty list, so a typo in a later caller looks like no branches.

seeds.title: argparse accepts abbreviated flags and a repeated --kind
seeds.detail: list --kin slice and list --rep <repo> succeed, and a repeated --kind uses the last value. Set allow_abbrev=False if exact flags are wanted.

seeds.title: list uses %(refname), not the spec's %(refname:short)
seeds.detail: The code strips refs/heads/ from the full ref name. The result is the same except where a tag shares a branch name. The plan allowed this.

seeds.title: testkit: no helper to create many refs in one repo
seeds.detail: The property test creates refs with git update-ref --stdin in its own file. A shared helper would speed other verifiers.

seeds.title: parse accepts non-ASCII digits in run and attempt tails
seeds.detail: Python \d matches Unicode digits, so sdlc/run-١ and sdlc/S-001-attempt-１２ parse as run n=1 and attempt n=12 and list next to sdlc/run-1. Two branches then claim one n, and name(run, n=1) does not return the listed branch. The spec writes the regex as \d+, so this follows the text and no requirement forbids it. Fix: use [0-9]+ or re.ASCII for the numeric parts in PARSE_ROWS.

title: evaluate applies one rule to a sample
riskReason: evaluate feeds the pre-flight verdict; a wrong True launches names a rule rejects.

seeds.title: Non-string pattern or odd regex raises instead of None
seeds.detail: Forge rules cross a trust boundary. A missing or non-string pattern raises TypeError. RecursionError or OverflowError from re.compile also escapes. Catch these in _raw_result and return None, or have S-012 catch them, to keep the never-block rule of R-035.

seeds.title: Regex backtracking can hang evaluate
seeds.detail: A pattern with catastrophic backtracking runs without limit. The plan accepts this risk because patterns come from the forge. Record it for S-012 to S-014.

seeds.title: Rule helpers sit in the name section
seeds.detail: Move evaluate and regex_error next to the rule code that S-012 and S-014 add, away from the name builders.

seeds.title: Pattern compiles twice
seeds.detail: regex_error and _raw_result each compile the pattern. Share one compile helper if it matters later.

seeds.title: Non-string pattern raises TypeError
seeds.detail: evaluate does not guard a rule whose pattern is not a string. Rules come from read_rules, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: T-R-072a overlaps T-R-033a and T-R-034a
seeds.detail: T-R-072a repeats the hit and miss checks of the four operators and the negate flip that T-R-033a and T-R-034a already pin. Its unique parts are the two bad patterns and the negate flip for regex. The spec names this test for R-072, so keeping it is acceptable. Optional fix: leave the bad-pattern cases here and drop the repeated operator cases.

seeds.title: No gap for exotic regex errors
seeds.detail: No test covers a pattern that raises RecursionError or OverflowError. The plan accepts this risk. No action needed.

seeds.title: evaluate raises on a rule with a missing or non-string pattern
seeds.detail: A starts_with rule with pattern None raises TypeError. A non-string sample also raises. The spec defines no such input, and the callers build rules. S-013 and S-014 should check that read_rules always gives string patterns.

seeds.title: evaluate raises OverflowError and RecursionError for some regex patterns
seeds.detail: x{99999999999999999999} raises OverflowError and 100000 nested groups raise RecursionError out of evaluate and regex_error on Python 3.14. The plan accepts this because only re.error is caught. S-012 and S-013 must catch them or the pre-flight crashes. A forge RE2 ruleset never holds such a pattern, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: evaluate raises on non-string pattern, sample or rule
seeds.detail: None or number patterns and samples raise TypeError or AttributeError. contains with a list sample returns True. The slice promises None for an unknown kind only. read_rules in S-014 must make rules with string patterns.

seeds.title: regex rules have no time limit
seeds.detail: The pattern (a+)+$ on 27 a characters then ! takes 4.8 s, and the time doubles per extra character. Branch samples are short and patterns come from the forge, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: One 120 s timeout in the first run of the hostile-input test did not reproduce
seeds.detail: Two later runs of the same payload finished in 40 ms. The cause is unknown and probably host load. No claim is made about it.

seeds.title: evaluate can hang on a nested-quantifier regex
seeds.detail: (a+)+$ on 40 'a' plus 'b' did not finish in 8 s. Plan accepts this; the spec states no limit. Hand to verify-limits.

seeds.title: evaluate raises on non-string input or a non-dict rule
seeds.detail: TypeError for non-string pattern or sample (38 of 40 calls), AttributeError for a non-dict rule, TypeError for regex without pattern. S-013 and S-014 callers must pass strings or wrap evaluate.

notes: Re-plan from scratch with the simplest approach; read failures.md. R-026 moved to S-014.

title: sample verdicts, bad patterns and check-ref-format
riskReason: A wrong aggregation passes a sample that a rule or check-ref-format rejects.

title: read_rules reads GitHub branch name patterns
riskReason: The GitHub read decides the verdict from a live API; a wrong mapping hides an active rule.

title: read_rules reads the GitLab push rule and the no-forge case
riskReason: A misread push rule hides the one GitLab constraint and passes names it rejects.

title: preflight tests the mode's branch names and prints a verdict
riskReason: The verdict gates launch; a wrong ok pushes the rejection the spec exists to prevent, though the push reports it.

title: preflight derives a format from one simple rule
riskReason: A wrong derivation writes a format the rule still rejects, and the run launches with it.

title: preflight edge cases and the forge shim suite
riskReason: The shim suite guards the unknown-rules paths; a wrong pass hides rules that will reject the push.

title: SKILL.md: the flag, the pre-flight bullet and the launch arg
riskReason: The driver prompt gates every launch; a wrong bullet ends runs early or skips the check.

title: SKILL.md names the run branch and checks the user's branch
riskReason: The rename check blocks a first run on a false match, or misses a collision and breaks resume.

title: sdlc-loop.js names branches through the format
riskReason: The loop script names verifier branches; a mismatch with the module breaks verification plumbing.

title: next-action.py recognizes branches through parse
riskReason: next-action drives every slice decision from branch state; a wrong parse resumes the wrong slice.

title: state-write.py names and classifies branches through the module
riskReason: state-write creates slice and milestone branches; a wrong name puts a pull request on the wrong base.

title: state-write.py threads the format through its remaining paths
riskReason: The threaded format touches every state-write branch path, including the loop-economy matchers.

title: janitor.py sweeps only verify branches through parse
riskReason: The janitor deletes local branches; a wrong parse deletes a run or attempt branch the loop still needs.

title: _common.md: the Branch names section and the first placeholders
riskReason: The prompts steer every agent; a wrong command in the table misdirects the loop's agents.

title: _common.md completes the placeholder table
riskReason: The remaining placeholder rows steer milestone, e2e, state and attempt branch naming.

title: every prompt replaces its branch literals with placeholders
riskReason: The sweep rewrites about twenty prompts; a wrong replacement misdirects one role at run time.

title: prompt tests guard the placeholders and the format records
riskReason: Test-only additions; the worst case is a failing test.

title: README documents the flag and the branch names
riskReason: Documentation only; no runtime reader.
